epics.title: High-Fidelity Visual Asset Sourcing and Delivery
epics.jtbd: When a visitor lands on the site, I want to see studio-quality imagery of the author that loads instantly, so that the site feels premium and performs optimally.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) and image payload size reduction
epics.tocConstraintRef: Network bandwidth and client rendering speed
requirements: R1: Source raw frame captures from the official YouTube channel (@dmitrii.efremov).
R2: Enhance and regenerate the raw frames using AI upscaling to achieve clean, studio-quality visuals.
R3: Encode all resulting images into modern WebP and AVIF formats with compression that maintains perceptual sharpness.
R4: Generate adaptively scaled variants (e.g., mobile, tablet, desktop resolutions) for each image asset.
R5: Implement responsive picture elements in the frontend to load the optimal image format and size for the visitor's device.
R6: Replace all legacy image assets and references across the existing site pages with the new optimized components.

slices.title: AI Frame Enhancement and Preparation
slices.jtbd: When implementing R1 and R2 for this epic, I want to extract and upscale YouTube frames using AI, so that studio-quality source images are available for encoding.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a set of raw frames from the specified YouTube channel
When the AI enhancement pipeline processes them
Then the output images must exhibit studio-quality sharpness without artifacts
Given the enhanced images
When saved to the source asset directory
Then they are ready for multi-format encoding.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Source image quality and AI processing time
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Percentage of frames meeting studio-quality visual acceptance criteria

slices.title: Automated Asset Encoding Pipeline
slices.jtbd: When implementing R3 and R4 for this epic, I want to automatically encode and scale source images into WebP and AVIF, so that lightweight variants are ready for delivery.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a studio-quality source image
When the encoding script runs
Then it must generate WebP and AVIF variants at defined breakpoint widths (e.g., 375px, 768px, 1440px)
Given the generated variants
When comparing file sizes
Then the total payload must be significantly reduced while maintaining sharpness.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Average byte size per delivered asset variant

slices.title: Responsive Picture Component Implementation
slices.jtbd: When implementing R5 and R6 for this epic, I want to build a responsive Svelte component and replace legacy images, so that the browser automatically downloads the most efficient format and scale.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the generated WebP and AVIF variants
When a visitor opens the site on a mobile device
Then the browser must request only the mobile-scaled AVIF or WebP variant
Given the picture component
When rendered in the DOM
Then it must include descriptive alt text for WCAG 2.1 level AA compliance
Given the existing site pages
When reviewing the source code
Then all legacy image references must be replaced with the new picture component.

slices.title: Visual Asset Delivery QA and Performance Audit
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to verify image loading behavior across the test pyramid, so that instant loading and quality are guaranteed.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the implemented picture component
When executing integration tests
Then the component must successfully resolve all AVIF and WebP source paths
Given the fully assembled frontend
When running an E2E performance audit (e.g., Lighthouse)
Then the image elements must score optimally for LCP and CLS without serving oversized assets
Given a mobile viewport test
When capturing screenshots
Then the layout must be visually verified and saved to .eneik/records/design-check.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Test execution time and visual validation
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Defect escape rate for layout shifts and unoptimized images
